inputs.prompt: ONE original young armoured warden, the Basalt Warden, facing screen right in elevated three-quarter view. Keep the youthful face, the shoulder-length dark brown hair, the grey scarf and layered grey tabard, the black iron plate armour, the brown leather straps and pouches, and the armoured boots. Exactly two arms, two hands and two legs. The screen-LEFT hand holds ONE short mace with an angular dark metal head; the screen-RIGHT arm carries ONE tall black cracked basalt pavise shield with an angular split top and copper bands. Preserve the mace, the basalt shield and the proportions. A steady, watchful idle that loops. The warden breathes, the shoulders rise and fall, the mace turns a little in the low hand, the shield settles on the arm, the head turns slightly to scan and the scarf stirs, then everything returns smoothly to the original stance. Both boots stay planted. No walking and no attack. Only the body moves; nothing else appears in the frame. Locked orthographic camera, fixed anatomical scale and centred body. Keep the full head, mace, the whole shield, limbs and boots within frame. The background is perfectly flat saturated BLUE throughout, no gradients or changes of hue. The blue background stays the same flat saturated blue in every frame and never darkens, flashes or changes colour. No scenery, floor shadow, camera motion, zoom, additional weapons, dust, sparks, motion trails, particles or extra limbs. Articulate joints naturally with physical planted-foot support; the shield stays a rigid stone slab and never morphs.
